persona: Friendly and a little apologetic about claiming late. Got a glazier's quote in August and has not noticed that it has since run out; has two photos of the cracked panel.
initial_message: Hi, I need to make a claim for a cracked glass door at our house. On Sunday 9 August my son's football hit the fixed glass panel of our lounge ranch slider and it cracked right across. Nobody was hurt and the door still locks. I got a quote from a glazier in August but I've only just got round to claiming.

facts.incident.description: My son was kicking a football in the back garden and it hit the fixed glass panel of the lounge ranch slider. The glass cracked from the bottom left corner right across the panel but stayed in the frame. I put clear tape along the crack.
facts.incident.cause: A football kicked in the back garden hit the glass
facts.loss.description: Fixed double-glazed panel of the lounge ranch slider cracked diagonally across the whole pane; the frame and the sliding panel are not damaged
property.affected_areas: lounge ranch slider, fixed glass panel
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: Taped along the crack and kept the children away from that side of the door
facts.policyholder.name: Tane Kilnhurst
facts.evidence.photos: Two photos taken on the day: the whole cracked panel, and a close-up of where the ball hit. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Karaka Worth Glazing dated 12 August 2026, total $2,139.00 including GST. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_quote_validity: I hadn't noticed it had a valid-until date. I can ask the glazier for an updated quote; they said that takes a few days.
facts.if_asked_why_the_claim_is_late: I was away for work for most of August and early September and it slipped my mind.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo from inside a lounge looking at the tall fixed glass panel of a dark aluminium sliding door that opens onto a back garden. A long crack runs diagonally across the whole double-glazed panel from the bottom left corner to the upper right, with a strip of clear tape stuck along the lower part of the crack. Green lawn and a timber fence outside, afternoon daylight. The frame shows the cracked glass panel and its dark aluminium frame.
materials.purpose: Shows the cracked fixed panel of the ranch slider

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone close-up of the bottom left corner of a double-glazed glass door panel in a dark aluminium frame, showing a small star-shaped impact point with short cracks radiating out and one long crack running up diagonally out of the frame. A faint round muddy scuff mark on the outside of the glass where a ball hit it. Daylight, lawn blurred in the background.
materials.purpose: Shows where the ball hit the glass

design.notes: The glazier's quote is dated 12 August 2026 and valid until 11 September 2026, before 1 October 2026, so it has expired. It is still after the incident, so the quote-date check is clear.

triage.rationale: The only repair quote passed its validity date (11 September 2026), so an updated quote is needed and someone must follow it up. The glass is cracked but intact and taped, nobody is hurt and the home is habitable, so nothing is complex. The amount (NZD 2,139.00 including GST) is under 5,000. Reporting late is not a triage reason. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

quote_before_loss.basis: Quote dated 12 August 2026; incident 9 August 2026. Its expiry does not affect the date check.

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (10 February 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2016-02-10, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
